item.title: MikroTik patches flaws currently being exploited to take over routers
item.description:
MikroTik fixed exploitable flaws in their router OS, currently under attack in the wild. Addressing these issues promptly is vital to prevent unauthorized control over devices. Still, not all users promptly apply updates, leaving many systems vulnerable.
— via CSO Online

item.title: Digital sovereignty, infrastructure and credential formats colliding
item.description:
Credential formats are facing new pressures amid debates on digital sovereignty. Moving from physical ID documents to digital credentials is a growing trend. The challenge: transitioning without a solid cryptographic foundation is risky and complex.
— via Biometric Update

item.title: Revolut confirms customer data breach, falling for fake government requests
item.description:
Revolut fell victim to a data breach from fake government requests for customer data. This underscores the vulnerability of relying on official-looking requests without proper verification. The catch: it shows how social engineering can bypass even sophisticated security measures.
— via Hacker News

item.title: CISA Adds 5 Actively Exploited Artifactory, ScreenConnect, and RouterOS Flaws to KEV
item.description:
CISA identified five new vulnerabilities in widely used systems like JFrog Artifactory. These flaws are actively exploited, requiring urgent patching. But the issue is many organizations may not yet have detected their exposure to these vulnerabilities.
— via The Hacker News

item.title: Public sector joins digital identity export market as countries package DPI capacity
item.description:
Public sectors worldwide are packaging their digital identity solutions for export. This promotes international collaboration on digital identity systems. The hurdle: adapting solutions to differing legal and technical standards globally.
— via Biometric Update

item.title: Attackers use passkey-themed scams to hijack Microsoft 365 accounts
item.description:
Scammers use passkey-themed lures to target Microsoft 365 users. These scams effectively deceive employees by impersonating IT personnel to gain account access. The limitation: even with better training, human error remains hard to totally eliminate.
— via CSO Online

item.title: Ant International, Visa, Mastercard work to make agentic protocols interoperable
item.description:
Visa, Mastercard, and Ant International aim for interoperability in agentic protocols. This could streamline onboarding for digital wallets and payments. The barrier: integrating these protocols across different ecosystems without disruption can be complex.
— via Biometric Update

item.title: Digital ID policy was scrapped, but government’s access challenges remain
item.description:
Despite scrapping a digital ID policy, the UK government still faces access hurdles. This affects the modernization of public service access. The roadblock: inconsistent approaches and changing policies hinder progress.
— via Identity Week

item.title: SpyCloud 2026 Identity Threat Report Finds Non-Human Identities Are Now the Leading Path into the Enterprise
item.description:
Non-human identities are now a major route for breaches into enterprises. This finding from SpyCloud's report highlights overlooked AI and machine identity risks. The downside: most organizations overestimate their monitoring capabilities in this area.
— via CSO Online

item.title: Your Critical Vulnerabilities Might Not Be Your Biggest Risk
item.description:
A post argues that critical vulnerabilities might not always pose the biggest risks. It suggests focusing on vulnerabilities with real pathways to compromise. The challenge: prioritizing effectively without under-placing serious vulnerabilities.
— via The Hacker News

item.title: AI agents exploited PaperCut flaws to breach 395 organizations
item.description:
AI agents played a pivotal role in exploiting PaperCut software flaws across organizations. The automated process significantly breaches security perimeters efficiently. Mitigation is difficult as AI-driven attacks evolve faster than detection tools.
— via Help Net Security

item.title: Trezor: 347,000 users targeted in phishing attacks after Brevo breach
item.description:
Phishing attacks following a breach targeted Trezor users. It once again shows how breaches of one service can impact others. The catch: even with phishing awareness, email-based attacks remain a prevalent threat.
— via BleepingComputer

item.title: Infostealer Logs Expose Replayable AI Tokens That Can Bypass MFA
item.description:
Infostealer logs reveal vulnerabilities in AI tokens that can bypass MFA. This reflects on how poorly protected tokens can lead to significant breaches. The core issue: security tokens remain vulnerable if stored or transmitted insecurely.
— via The Hacker News

item.title: BigBear phishing crew nets thousands of Microsoft 365 credentials
item.description:
The BigBear phishing group collected significant Microsoft 365 credentials. More than just a statistic, it shows the ongoing effectiveness of tried-and-true phishing. The problem: uncovering how these credentials are being exploited is an ongoing task.
— via The Register Security

item.title: Elevating identity governance: from ecosystem silos to enterprise control
item.description:
The call is for better identity governance, moving beyond siloed ecosystems. It's a push towards enterprise-wide identity control. The limitation: integration challenges between legacy systems and new governance models.
— via SailPoint

item.title: Passkey-themed phishing attacks lead to Microsoft 365 data theft
item.description:
Phishing attackers are using passkey and single sign-on themes to steal Microsoft 365 data. It highlights how even modern authentication methods can be harnessed for social engineering. The catch: businesses using passkeys must ensure that their workforce is fully aware of these new attack angles.
— via BleepingComputer

item.title: Unico acquires biometrics provider Valida, gaining entry into Argentina market
item.description:
Unico acquires Valida, gaining a foothold in Argentina's biometric verification market. This move increases Unico's regional presence, impacting identity verification across Latin America. The catch: if you're not in or expanding to the region, this acquisition has limited direct relevance.
— via Biometric Update

item.title: KPMG investment in Reality Defender backs hiring spree to fight deepfakes
item.description:
KPMG invests in Reality Defender to tackle deepfakes. This means an improvement in fraud prevention capabilities through advanced deepfake detection. Yet, the tech is part of KPMG's managed services, so benefits are tied to engaging with them.
— via Biometric Update

item.title: Florida says motor vehicle data breach tied to credentials stolen from officer’s personal device
item.description:
A Florida DMV data breach traces back to a stolen police account credential. It underscores how unmanaged personal devices pose risks to sensitive systems. Note: this reinforces the need for strict device and credential management protocols.
— via The Record

item.title: Digital ID for alcohol sales is coming to the UK: hear what it means for the identity sector
item.description:
UK sets the stage for digital IDs in alcohol sales. This is a key move for age verification technology and digital ID acceptance. The missing piece: true adoption timelines can vary, depending on regulatory and industry alignment.
— via Biometric Update

item.title: Florida confirms DMV database breached via stolen police account
item.description:
Florida DMV breach exploited a stolen police account credential. Demonstrates the risks when personal devices aren't secure enough for storing credentials. Reminder: single-account compromise can threaten entire systems.
— via BleepingComputer

item.title: Phishing Research Challenges Conventional Security Awareness Testing
item.description:
New research questions traditional security awareness testing by focusing on credential leak measurement over click rates. The need to track what really happens after a phishing email lands is clear. But organizations must still deploy broader training alongside new measurements.
— via SecurityWeek

item.title: IDScan confirms breach after 153 million driver’s licenses leak on dark web
item.description:
IDScan admits to a breach that exposed 153 million driver’s licenses, highlighting data protection issues. If you rely on a third party for ID verification, it’s a cautionary tale of diligence and vendor selection. But, the scope affects primarily their customer base.
— via Help Net Security

item.title: Trezor Says 347,000 Users Received Phishing Emails After Brevo Hack
item.description:
Post-Brevo hack, Trezor warns about phishing emails to 347,000 users. Highlights the ripple effects of third-party service breaches on customer communication safety. Immediate measure: monitoring email campaigns for unauthorized uses.
— via SecurityWeek

item.title: ConnectWise patches critical ScreenConnect authentication failure after five days
item.description:
ConnectWise patches a critical ScreenConnect vulnerability related to user permissions. Quick fixes were essential since unauthorized file transfers could have serious consequences. Yet, dependent users need to actively apply patches for protection.
— via CSO Online

item.title: Cisco FMC Flaws Exploited to Steal Credentials and Deploy Qilin Ransomware
item.description:
Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center suffers from exploited vulnerabilities leading to credential theft. Highlights the stakes with any authentication bypass flaw when mitigations aren't timely. Effective defense is contingent on prompt patch deployment.
— via The Hacker News

item.title: Artifactory flaws chained in attacks deploying backdoor malware
item.description:
JFrog Artifactory vulnerabilities were chained to deploy malware via backdoor access. Admin access through bypassed authentication systems is a significant threat. The pivotal action point: ensure you’re up-to-date on patches.
— via BleepingComputer

item.title: In Other News: InjectEave Attack, SIM Swapper Sentenced, Glasswing Findings Review
item.description:
Various under-the-radar security stories, including bypassed phishing filters using invisible Unicode. Reinforces how sophisticated phishing can bypass current defenses. The challenge remains to keep awareness high for evolving tactics.
— via SecurityWeek

item.title: Synced Passkeys in Microsoft Entra for Phishing-resistant MFA
item.description:
Microsoft Entra introduces synced passkeys for more phishing-resistant MFA. This simplifies managing secure sign-in methods across devices for better user experiences. It’s still dependent on having up-to-date Microsoft environments.
— via Microsoft Entra

item.title: Companies may be measuring phishing resilience the wrong way
item.description:
A report suggests companies may be assessing phishing resilience incorrectly by focusing on click rates alone. The takeaway is to also track credential submission rates for a true measure of risk. The challenge is shifting internal metrics that may overlook these insights.
— via Help Net Security

item.title: AI agents change the identity security question in the middle of enterprises’ answer
item.description:
AI agents are emerging as a new cybersecurity challenge, particularly for digital identity. They complicate authentication processes and demand more secure identity governance. The complication is integrating these layers without slowing down enterprise operations.
— via Biometric Update

item.title: For EU consumers, trust in EUDI Wallet will need to be earned over time: IDnow
item.description:
IDnow reports that EU consumers may struggle to trust the EUDI Wallet as rollout continues. Trust issues could hinder adoption of these digital ID solutions. The trouble lies in overcoming widespread privacy and security concerns before the year-end deadline.
— via Biometric Update

item.title: The next bottleneck for African digital identity is infrastructure, not software
item.description:
Infrastructure, not software, is now the bottleneck for African digital identity deployment. Expanded infrastructure is necessary for more effective digital identity solutions. The setback is that infrastructure projects often take years to complete.
— via Biometric Update

item.title: Your passkeys can now move between password managers on Android
item.description:
Google enables transferring passkeys between password managers on Android without needing to download files. This makes switching managers less risky for users. Now, it depends on password manager support for this feature to function seamlessly.
— via Help Net Security

item.title: GLEIF welcomes eMudhra as a validation agent
item.description:
The GLEIF organization has named eMudhra a validation agent in India. This integration simplifies processes for Legal Entity Identifier management. However, the benefit is specific to organizations using eMudhra's services.
— via Identity Week

item.title: IDScan confirms breach tied to 153 million stolen driver’s licenses
item.description:
IDScan confirmed a breach compromising 153 million driver’s licenses. This is significant for identity verification processes relying on scanned documents. The flaw is rooted in stored data security, highlighting the need for stringent access controls.
— via BleepingComputer

item.title: Implementer’s Draft of OpenID Connect Key Binding Approved
item.description:
The OpenID Foundation has approved the Key Binding Implementer’s Draft. This sets a key binding standard that enhances the security framework for OpenID Connect. The caveat is it's a draft, so it may not yet be supported by all implementations.
— via OpenID Foundation

item.title: SC Media: Why yesterday’s identity security standards no longer work for banks
item.description:
Banks are reconsidering their identity security standards due to new challenges from AI and cyber threats. These outdated standards may not suffice, demanding a shift towards more robust identity solutions. The issue: financial institutions must navigate complex regulatory landscapes before implementing change.
— via FIDO Alliance

item.title: SoulAuth: An Actor-native Identity Architecture and Rust Reference Implementation for Humans and Long-lived AI Actors
item.description:
A paper introduces SoulAuth, a Rust implementation for managing long-lived AI actors. It addresses identity persistence for humans and AI over time. However, it's a conceptual framework, limited by its current applicability to specific tech stacks.
— via arXiv

item.title: Attackers are weaponizing the gap between Chromium fixes and Chrome patches
item.description:
New gap-exploiting attacks highlight the risks between Chromium fixes and Chrome patches. These gaps are exploited for spear phishing via an exploit kit named BlueMoon. The catch: users and IT teams must apply patches as soon as they are released to minimize risk.
— via CSO Online

item.title: Deep-Fake CAPTCHA: Mitigating Next-Generation Social Engineering Attacks
item.description:
The DF-CAPTCHA framework offers a defense against real-time deepfake attacks during calls. By requiring challenge-response tasks, it makes impersonation harder. The limitation is that it may not cover all deepfake techniques yet.
— via arXiv

item.title: AI workflows may be creating a dangerous new authorization blind spot
item.description:
AI workflows might be opening a new authorization gap, termed 'workflow identity hijacking.' This makes it critical for firms to audit their identity and access processes. The tricky part is ensuring all entry points are adequately protected against unauthorized actions.
— via CSO Online

item.title: When an AI Agent Acts on Behalf of a Resident
item.description:
AI agents challenge the assumption that an acting person is the one interacting with services. This raises new questions regarding identity verification and authorization. The issue lies in adapting current frameworks to ensure accurate identity proofing with AI involvement.
— via Spruce ID

item.title: Cybercriminals are building phishing pages that exist only inside victims’ browsers
item.description:
Phishing pages are being crafted directly inside victims' browsers using blob URLs. This attack method bypasses traditional web server delivery, making detection harder and exploiting the trust users have in their own browsers. The catch: defense requires focusing on browser-level security measures and user education about content origins.
— via Help Net Security

item.title: Federal regulators say mDLs can be used for bank identity checks
item.description:
U.S. regulators cleared mobile driver’s licenses (mDLs) for verifying bank account holders. This allows financial institutions to streamline onboarding with digital IDs, moving away from physical documents. The limitation: mDLs need widespread issuer support and updated bank systems to become practical.
— via Biometric Update

item.title: Trezor warns users of email provider breach, phishing attacks
item.description:
Trezor warns users about phishing attacks following a breach of their email provider. Users are targeted through deceptive emails leveraging trust from Trezor’s own branding. The issue here is broad: if your contact details are compromised, phishing can escalate quickly.
— via BleepingComputer

item.title: Product showcase: GitGuardian Honeytoken catches credential theft as it happens
item.description:
GitGuardian's new honeytoken product detects credential theft in real time. By placing fake credentials in places attackers are likely to scan, it offers a chance to catch intruders early. It's effective only if decoys are indistinguishable from real data and properly managed.
— via Help Net Security

item.title: RAND warns security biometrics, digital ID can become tools for targeting
item.description:
RAND warns that digital IDs and biometrics can lead to targeting if misused. Security systems need checks and balances to prevent tools from being repurposed for surveillance. The honest risk: these recommendations often clash with regional laws and actual practice.
— via Biometric Update

item.title: France expands digital identity access in overseas territories
item.description:
France extends digital identity access to overseas territories. This lets users activate their digital IDs through local apps with QR code validation. It only works if local infrastructure is equipped to handle and verify these digital IDs reliably.
— via Biometric Update

item.title: Cisco confirms CVE-2026-20079 Secure FMC flaw exploited in attacks
item.description:
A severe Cisco Secure FMC flaw, CVE-2026-20079, is being exploited live. Attackers bypass authentication, posing a real threat to network management systems if unpatched. Fixes or mitigations rely on swift patch deployment, which isn’t always instantly feasible.
— via BleepingComputer

item.title: MFA's Weakest Link: Account Recovery Is the New Attack Path
item.description:
MFA-protected accounts are targeted via weak recovery processes. Recovery workflows are being exploited, creating a new vector for account takeovers. Despite MFA, securing recovery processes remains critical to thwarting these attacks.
— via BleepingComputer

item.title: Show HN: Compute polynomials twice as fast
item.description:
A new method speeds up polynomial computation, potentially affecting hashing algorithms. This could change how fast certain cryptographic processes are, benefiting digital-identity systems reliant on rapid hashing. The method is proven, but needs adoption across libraries and platforms to matter.
— via Hacker News

item.title: AI adoption brings new security headaches for already stretched CISOs
item.description:
AI adoption burdens CISOs with new security challenges without extra resources. Identity systems are under stress as threat models evolve around AI access and data manipulation. The risk increases but adapting depends heavily on team bandwidth and specific AI policy tools.
— via Help Net Security
